text: fit_logistic() fits binary, proportional-odds ordinal, generalized-logit nominal outcome models. Clinically meaningful levels always explicit; factor storage order never decides event, order, reference category. Every model-producing result four slots: $data: patient-level data predictions scores; $meta: formula, declared levels, model family, row accounting, package versions, bundle_version = 1L; $tables: estimates, covariance, by_imputation, fit_status, plus workflow-specific diagnostics; $models: every fitted model, including every imputation-specific fit. estimates table columns term, estimate, std.error, statistic, df, p.value, conf.low, conf.high, odds_ratio, pooled. Count models (bs_count()) name exponentiated column rate_ratio, since log-link coefficient exponentiates rate ratio. by_imputation imputation, term, estimate, std.error; fit_status imputation, converged, n_input, n_analyzed, n_excluded. stacked imputations, patient predictions averaged across fits coefficients covariance use Rubin’s rules. Missing patients, changed categorical predictor levels, aliased terms, non-convergence, unusable covariance matrices stop analysis instead producing partial pool. validate_logistic() applies saved version-1 binary bundle declared validation cohort without refitting. reports calibration, observed versus expected events, AUC, Brier score. Ordinal nominal validation part first interface.

what: hvtiRpropensity: Propensity Score Methods for Cardiac Surgery Studies — hvtiRpropensity-package
title: hvtiRpropensity: Propensity Score Methods for Cardiac Surgery Studies — hvtiRpropensity-package
text: Provides functions propensity score balancing score analysis used cardiac surgery comparative-effectiveness research.  Translates Cleveland Clinic HVTI SAS template library consistent R workflow. Step 1: estimate scores: ps_logistic(): binary treatment propensity score (logistic regression; supports multiply-imputed data via stacked data frame). ps_forest(): binary treatment propensity score random forest (randomForestSRC), scored --bag. ps_ordinal(): ordered treatment propensity score (proportional-odds model via MASS::polr; equivalent SAS PROC LOGISTIC default ordinal responses). ps_nominal(): nominal treatment propensity score (multinomial logistic via nnet::multinom; equivalent SAS PROC LOGISTIC link=glogit). bs_continuous(): balancing score continuous exposure (linear regression; equivalent SAS PROC REG + %grp macro). bs_count(): balancing score count exposure (negative-binomial Poisson regression; equivalent SAS PROC GENMOD dist=nb). Outcome models: fit_logistic(): binary, ordinal nominal outcome-model bundle, Rubin pooling stacked imputations Barnard-Rubin degrees freedom, matching mice::pool(). fit_linear(): linear outcome-model bundle, Rubin pooling. validate_logistic(): applies saved binary bundle validation cohort without refitting. Step 2: balance use scores: ps_match(): 1:1 nearest-neighbour matching pre-computed score, probability logit scale. scale = "logit", caliper_sd = 0.2 Austin (2011) caliper. Returns pair_id column $data use sa_rosenbaum() ps_rmst(). ps_weight(): IPTW weights (ATE / ATT / ATC) pre-computed score. ps_support(): compares common-support trimming rules. ps_rmst(): restricted mean survival contrast, weighted, matched pairs ps_match() object. Balance statistics: ps_stddiff(): standardized differences variable type, optionally weighted (CCF %stddiff). ps_stddiff_perm(): permutation reference differences (CCF %stddiffci). ps_mw_var(): matching-weight difference means bootstrap SD (CCF %mw_var). Step 3: sensitivity analysis (optional): sa_rosenbaum(): Rosenbaum gamma bounds matched analyses; much hidden bias overturn result. sa_evalue(): E-values (VanderWeele & Ding 2017) unmeasured confounding. Odds hazard ratios need rare. sa_overlap(): overlap positivity diagnostics score distribution. sa_trim_sweep(): effective sample size weights change across IPTW trim thresholds. Data: sample_ps_data(), sample_ps_data_ordinal(), sample_ps_data_nominal() sample_ps_data_count() generate synthetic datasets; is_ps_data() tests ps_data object. Every function except four data generators (return data frames) is_ps_data() returns ps_data S3 object. $data slot holds input data score, weight flag columns appended, $meta records columns parameters used, $tables holds diagnostics: SMD tables, group counts, effective sample sizes, sensitivity function's bounds sweeps. hvtiPlotR::hv_mirror_hist() reads $data ps_match() ps_weight() object directly. hvtiPlotR::hv_balance() read $tables : needs one long data frame variable, group std_diff columns, difference percent, SMD tables stacked multiplied 100 first. vignette shows reshape. SAS programs package ports ship , system.file("sas-templates", package = "hvtiRpropensity").
